name: Nimble Robotics
desc: Runs AI-driven robotic e-commerce fulfillment centres as a third-party logistics service for retail and consumer brands.
markets: US fulfillment sites only (Indianapolis, Bay Area, Southern California, Dallas, Atlanta, New Jersey planned); FedEx alliance targets a US national network.
rationale: US-focused B2B logistics operator; F1's growing US audience offers some hospitality value, but limited brand marketing need.

name: Nxera
desc: Singtel's data centre business, offering colocation and AI-ready data centre capacity to enterprises and hyperscalers in South-East Asia.
markets: Operating capacity in Singapore; joint-venture data centres in Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia; no verified presence outside South-East Asia.
rationale: Regional B2B infrastructure brand; F1 Singapore Grand Prix hospitality could suit enterprise customer entertainment, but reach is narrow.
changed: Launched as Singtel's data centre brand in 2024

name: Northern Data Group
desc: Provides GPU cloud computing and data centre capacity for AI developers and enterprises, now within Rumble's Quake AI unit.
markets: Large GPU estate in Europe; US parent RUM Group signed a multi-year capacity contract with US-based Together AI in 2026.
rationale: Now part of a US media and cloud group; technology tie-in possible, but B2B infrastructure with modest brand marketing.
changed: Acquired (about 85%) by Rumble, completed June 2026; parent renamed RUM Group Inc.

name: Tonal
desc: Makes a wall-mounted smart home gym with digital resistance, sold with a monthly workout membership to consumers.
markets: Sells and delivers in the United States only (including Hawaii and Alaska); no verified sales in Canada, UK or elsewhere.
rationale: Consumer fitness brand with performance-training message, but US-only sales limit the value of F1's global audience.

name: I-TRACING
desc: Provides cybersecurity consulting, integration and managed security services, including round-the-clock monitoring, to large organisations.
markets: France headquarters with subsidiaries in the UK, Switzerland, Canada (Montreal) and Hong Kong; also cited in Malaysia and China.
rationale: Growing European cyber services firm with Asia and Canada offices; B2B hospitality could support enterprise sales, though brand budget is modest.
changed: Backed by investment funds Oakley Capital, Eurazeo and Sagard NewGen

name: YipitData
desc: Sells alternative data and research on companies and sectors to investment funds and corporations by subscription.
markets: Offices across the US, Asia-Pacific (Hong Kong, Shanghai, Beijing, Guangzhou, Singapore) and India; clients include large investment funds.
rationale: Clients are hedge funds and asset managers; F1 B2B hospitality could suit client entertainment, but brand marketing is limited.
changed: Carlyle led a growth investment in 2021

name: Juniper Square
desc: Provides fund administration, investor management and accounting software and services for private-market fund managers.
markets: Customers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; offices in the US, Luxembourg, the UK and India.
rationale: Serves private equity and real-estate managers; F1 hospitality fits wealthy GP and LP audiences, but niche B2B brand.

name: Certn
desc: Provides online background screening, including criminal record, identity and employment checks, to employers and landlords.
markets: Canada and US, UK and EMEA (via Credence acquisition) and Australia (via InterCheck acquisition).
rationale: Mid-sized B2B HR services firm across three regions; weak consumer brand and limited reason for F1 spend.

name: Tieto
desc: Provides industry software and digital engineering and consulting services to banks, healthcare, public sector and industrial customers.
markets: Mainly Nordic customers (Finland, Sweden, Norway, Denmark), plus operations in DACH, Iberia, Central/Eastern Europe and the United States.
rationale: Listed Nordic tech group; F1 hospitality and technology storytelling could support enterprise sales in Europe and the US.
changed: Rebranded from Tietoevry to Tieto (announced November 2025); Tech Services sold to Agilitas in 2025, now Vivicta

name: Emergent
desc: Offers an AI agent platform that lets users without coding skills build and launch web and mobile apps.
markets: Most staff in Bengaluru, India, with a US office in San Francisco; sells online; customer geography not published.
rationale: Fast-growing consumer-facing AI tool with Indian and US roots; F1 could build brand awareness, though company is young.

name: Euclyd
desc: Designs energy-efficient AI inference chips and rack systems, called CRAFTWERK, for enterprise, government and hyperscale customers.
markets: Pre-revenue; based in the Netherlands, in talks with potential customers, first systems expected from 2028.
rationale: Pre-revenue chip developer backed by Samsung; technology tie-in possible later, but no product to market yet.

name: Gravis Robotics
desc: Develops autonomy systems that retrofit excavators and other heavy machines for construction and quarry contractors.
markets: Reported operations in seven countries across the UK, EU, US, Latin America and Asia; UK partners include Morgan Sindall and Flannery.
rationale: Engineering-led robotics firm; technology showcase possible, but early-stage B2B with small marketing budget.

name: Matic Robots
desc: Makes US-assembled autonomous robot vacuum and mop cleaners using on-device vision navigation, sold directly to consumers.
markets: Sells direct to consumers in the United States; no confirmed sales in other countries; Europe would need CE certification.
rationale: Young US consumer hardware brand; F1's US audience fits, but sales are US-only and marketing budget is small.

name: Turing
desc: Develops end-to-end AI driving models aimed at fully autonomous driving for carmakers' vehicles and robotaxis.
markets: Pre-revenue; development in Japan with partners such as Denso; system targeted for use from 2028.
rationale: Automotive AI start-up with a motorsport-friendly story, but pre-revenue and Japan-only; limited budget for F1.

name: Blitzy
desc: Sells an autonomous software development platform where AI agents modernise legacy code and build applications for large enterprises.
markets: Customers are mainly US Global 2000 enterprises; one listing shows a hiring location in Pune, India; no verified international sales.
rationale: Enterprise AI vendor; F1 hospitality could reach large-company buyers, but young B2B firm with US focus.

name: HappyRobot
desc: Sells AI agents that handle phone calls, emails and operational tasks for logistics firms such as freight brokers and carriers.
markets: Offices in San Francisco, Chicago and Madrid; reported presence across North America, Europe, Latin America and Australia; customers include DHL.
rationale: Fast-growing B2B AI vendor to logistics; F1 logistics and hospitality angle plausible, but young firm with niche buyers.

name: K1x
desc: Provides AI-based software that extracts and manages Schedule K-1, 1099 and W-2 tax data for investors and accounting firms.
markets: Serves US private-market investors, accounting firms and family offices around US tax forms; no verified international activity.
rationale: Niche US tax software for accountants and funds; little brand marketing need; weak F1 fit.
changed: Growth investment led by Sumeru Equity Partners in 2026

name: Obsidian Security
desc: Sells security software that protects SaaS applications, identities and AI agents for large enterprises.
markets: Staff in about ten countries including the US, UK, Canada, Argentina and Australia; Australian data centre; expansion into Germany.
rationale: Enterprise cybersecurity vendor; rivals such as CrowdStrike and Zscaler already sponsor F1, giving a clear B2B hospitality case.

name: Spur Intelligence
desc: Provides IP intelligence data that helps security, fraud and threat teams detect anonymised and obscured internet traffic.
markets: US-based; customer locations not published; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Small B2B security data provider with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Vecna Robotics
desc: Makes autonomous mobile robots such as tuggers and pallet jacks, plus fleet software, for warehouses and factories.
markets: Customers such as GEODIS and Shape Corp in the US; no verified operations outside the United States.
rationale: B2B warehouse automation firm with few customers; limited marketing culture; weak F1 fit.
changed: Spun off from Vecna Technologies in 2018

name: Code Metal
desc: Provides an AI platform that translates and verifies legacy code for embedded and edge hardware in defence and industry.
markets: Mainly US defence customers (US Air Force, L3Harris, RTX); Toshiba in Japan also reported; targeting automotive and semiconductors.
rationale: Defence-heavy AI software vendor; automotive target gives a small technology angle, but F1 fit is weak.

name: Nominal
desc: Sells software for collecting and analysing hardware test data for aerospace, defence, energy, robotics and automotive firms.
markets: US offices (Los Angeles, Austin, New York, Washington, Seattle) and London; about half of customers in defence.
rationale: Test-and-telemetry software has a natural F1 engineering showcase, though customers are mostly defence and the firm is young.

name: Whale
desc: Sells an AI operating system that uses camera and sensor data to run enterprise operations, with edge AI devices.
markets: Over 1,600 enterprise customers in more than 45 countries; expanding in North America and Asia-Pacific, targeting Middle East and Europe.
rationale: Asia-based AI firm expanding internationally; F1 races in Asia and the Gulf could support enterprise brand building.

name: WorkOS
desc: Provides authentication, single sign-on, directory sync and user management APIs for software companies selling to enterprises.
markets: US-based; named customers mainly US software and AI firms; one profile lists London and Mumbai offices, not confirmed.
rationale: Developer-focused B2B infrastructure; F1 hospitality has limited value for its buyers; weak to moderate fit.
